breaking_news.headline: FIFA has a new plan to raise billions of dollars: Selling stakes in the World Cup
breaking_news.summary: FIFA has a complex plan to sell chunks of its commercial rights to the World Cup to minority investors, including a firm run by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Jared Kushner.

breaking_news.headline: More Americans are going bankrupt. What does that mean?
breaking_news.summary: The bankruptcy rate has risen about 48% between 2022 and 2025, although it's still below pre-pandemic levels.

breaking_news.headline: A divided Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady despite high inflation
breaking_news.summary: The Federal Reserve left its benchmark interest rate unchanged Wednesday.  Fed policymakers say they remain committed to curbing stubborn inflation.

breaking_news.headline: The renter-owner wealth gap is wider than ever, as many are priced out of buying
breaking_news.summary: Housing has long been the largest source of wealth for middle income families. But many renters cannot afford to buy as housing prices soar, which could fuel a generational divide.

breaking_news.headline: The economy slowed a bit -- but Americans continued to spend
breaking_news.summary: The U.S. economy grew at an annual rate of 1.5% in the spring, according to the Commerce Department. That's a modest slowdown from the previous quarter — but consumer spending picked up steam.

breaking_news.headline: European soccer leaders to boycott  the World Cup in an unprecedented step
breaking_news.summary: European soccer associations said they would boycott the World Cup unless FIFA reverses a controversial deal to sell minority stakes to the marquee soccer tournament.

breaking_news.headline: Are you choosing to stay single? We want to hear from you
breaking_news.summary: Solo living, solo travel, and solo dining are all being embraced as more adults are choosing to remain single. Many Americans aren't interested in dating, and being single is a symbol of autonomy.

breaking_news.headline: Mortgage rates hit their highest level in a year, driven by war and inflation concerns
breaking_news.summary: The 30-year fixed-rate mortgage reached 6.66% on average Thursday.

breaking_news.headline: Spain sending troops as thousands enter enclave of Ceuta from Morocco
breaking_news.summary: At least 18 people drown as migrants try to swim to Spanish territory amid scenes of chaos at the border.

breaking_news.headline: UK rapper Yung Filly found not guilty of raping woman after Australian show
breaking_news.summary: The YouTuber has been found guilty for two counts of assault over the 2024 incident in Perth.

breaking_news.headline: Fifa says 'nobody selling football' as plan continues
breaking_news.summary: Football's governing body Fifa plans to continue the consultation process after Uefa threatens to boycott World Cups.

breaking_news.headline: Hundreds escape Greek wildfire by sea as blazes continue across Europe
breaking_news.summary: Around 500 people, mostly tourists, are evacuated by boat from Agios Vasileios after becoming trapped.

breaking_news.headline: Peru's ex-president has 15-year jail sentence for corruption charges overturned
breaking_news.summary: Ollanta Humala had been convicted of money laundering offences alongside his wife in 2025.

breaking_news.headline: AC Milan and Italy great Baresi dies aged 66
breaking_news.summary: AC Milan and Italy great Franco Baresi has died at the age of 66, the Italian club announces.

breaking_news.headline: If Hamas disarmament plan holds, it could mark first credible step to ending Gaza war
breaking_news.summary: The plan - if successful - potentially removes the most significant obstacle to advancing the Trump-backed peace initiative in Gaza.

breaking_news.headline: About 60,000 migrants arrive in Ceuta in 24 hours, Spanish territory's leader says
breaking_news.summary: Spain's prime minister described the situation as an "attack" on its North African territory and said all illegal migrants would be returned to Morocco.

breaking_news.headline: Thames Water boss says leakage targets 'not realistic'
breaking_news.summary: Chris Weston said Thames wanted "to do better" but some of its targets were not achievable.

breaking_news.headline: 'I pay £580 a month to live in a disused care home': Property guardians show us around
breaking_news.summary: Could you live communally in a disused building in exchange for a heavily discounted rent? Property guardians show us around.

breaking_news.headline: India wants to join the strawberry superpowers
breaking_news.summary: Indian strawberry farmers rely on varieties imported from the US and Europe, but that could change.

breaking_news.headline: BP puts North Sea business up for sale
breaking_news.summary: The decision follows a review of BP's operations and is set to end 60 years of production in the region by the oil giant.
